title: Streaming Schema Gatekeeper for Console Usage Events
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: The current console usage event pipeline accepts loosely typed JSON from multiple collectors (UI, SDKs, API proxies). Schema drift and malformed events cause downstream ETL failures, silent data loss in BigQuery, and expensive debug time. Goal: Implement a streaming 'Schema Gatekeeper' service that validates, normalizes, versions, and routes console usage events before they reach the main Kafka topics and downstream transformers. Scope: 1) Deploy a lightweight, horizontally scalable validation service that runs in the data plane close to collectors. 2) Integrate with a schema registry (self-hosted or Confluent-style) supporting semantic versioning and compatibility checks. 3) Provide configurable validation modes per-topic (reject, sanitize, accept-with-warning). 4) Emit rich metrics and tracing for rejected events, latency, and schema mismatch patterns. 5) Ensure idempotency and ordering guarantees required by the transformer stage. Acceptance criteria: - Gatekeeper validates >95% of event types with existing schemas in registry. - End-to-end validation latency added <10ms p95 for typical event payloads. - Rejected event rate below 0.1% in steady state for production traffic (after rollout). - Clear error codes and consumer-friendly dead-lettering strategy documented. Design notes: - Ingestion path: Collector -> Edge proxy -> Gatekeeper (validate & normalize) -> Kafka topic (validated.events.v1) -> transformer -> warehouse. - Validation implementation: fast JSON schema (ajv-like) compiled to wasm or optimized code paths; schema registry at /schemas with versions and compatibility rules. - Compatibility modes: backward-compatible (additive fields allowed), strict (no unknown fields), and permissive (warnings only). - Sanitization rules: drop PII fields per policy, trim oversized arrays, convert legacy enum values via mapper table. - Backpressure: Gatekeeper must apply bounded queues and return 429 to collectors when downstream Kafka lag exceeds threshold. - Observability: Prometheus metrics (validation_latency_ms, rejects_total, sanction_mode_total), logs with sampling, and OpenTelemetry spans. - Security: only internal clients with mTLS and token-based auth can publish; validation service enforces KMS-based key rotation for signing schema updates. - Rollout plan: Canary on 10% of traffic in us-east1 -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on rejects_total > 1% or validation_latency_ms p95 > 25ms. Migration: provide a compatibility shim to route legacy events to a 'legacy' topic while teams onboard to new schema. Risks / Tradeoffs: - Purely blocking validation reduces bad downstream data but could increase surface for outages; mitigation is permissive mode and canaries. - Strict runtime validation (full JS engine) is slower; prefer precompiled rules or WebAssembly to meet latency targets. Implementation tasks: - Schema registry API and UI endpoints (register, get, list, set-compatibility) - Gatekeeper service (gRPC + HTTP) with validation plugin architecture - Collector SDK updates to propagate schema version headers and client-side sampling of invalid events - DLQ Kafka topic and retention policy - Automated test harness with fuzzing for schema evolution corner cases - Dashboard in Console for per-schema health and rejected event inspection Documentation: - PRD: drive.redwood.com/console-analytics/schema-gatekeeper-prd (internal) - Design diagram: drive.redwood.com/diagrams/gatekeeper-arch.png - Initial API proto: github.com/redwood-inference/analytics-protos/pull/128
